# [STORY] As a user, I want to type or dictate a complex natural-language movie query, so that I can find movies by person, role, date range, and collaborators

## User Story
**As a** user
**I want** to type or dictate a complex natural-language movie query
**So that** I can find movies by person, role, date range, and collaborators without learning a filter UI

## Parent Epic
Parent: #195

## Acceptance Criteria (Given/When/Then)
- [x] Given a user types "movies Tom Hanks directed between 2000 and 2010", when they submit, then results are limited to movies matching person=Tom Hanks, role=directed, year range 2000-2010
- [x] Given a query includes a collaborator constraint ("...that also starred Meg Ryan"), when submitted, then results are further filtered to movies crediting that collaborator too
- [x] Given a query is just a plain title ("Inception"), when submitted, then ai-service's parser recognizes it as a plain title and the existing movie-service title search still returns the expected result, with no query-shape branching in the frontend
- [x] Given a user dictates the same kind of complex query via voice control instead of typing, when transcription completes, then it is parsed and executed through this same pipeline, not the old verbatim substring search
- [x] Given the natural-language parse fails or returns no confident filter, when that happens, then the frontend shows a clear message rather than silently returning an empty or wrong result set

## Notes
The ADR is `docs/architecture/adr/020-nl-query-cross-service-aggregation.md` (#201). Its review found that `role=DIRECTED`/`PRODUCED` and the `yearFrom`/`yearTo` range weren't actually servable by actor-service and movie-service as they stood — #217 and #218 closed those gaps before #202/#203 implementation started.

Scope note: "remove previously imposed guardrails" refers to the search bar being hard-wired to movie-service's title-only `/search`. It does not refer to `PromptSanitizer`, which is an anti-prompt-injection control and stays exactly as-is — the new endpoint still runs raw input through it before prompting Ollama.

Companion Stories: #199 layers live highlighting on this Story's parser output; #200 covers transcription accuracy separately. This Story only covers what happens to a transcript once VoiceControl has one.
